required_outcomes: Treats both issues as open again: the blocked toilet (the only toilet, so urgent) and the bedroom window.

Contacts the landlord promptly to say the toilet is blocked again and is the only toilet, pointing out that his email named Flat 18, 88 Alder Lane and asking him to confirm whether the plumber visit is for Flat 24, 150 Copperfield Walk and when it will be.
Asks the landlord how he wants the bedroom window handled (his own contractor or the agency’s).
Gives the tenant an honest update (the landlord has been asked about a plumber; no time confirmed) and sets a short review, the same or next working day, given there is no working toilet.
acceptable_alternatives: Phoning or texting the landlord as well as emailing, given the urgency.
Stating in the message to the landlord that, if his plumber is not attending Flat 24 today, the agency can send its own plumber and asking him to approve that.
positive_behaviours: Asks the tenant whether there is any other toilet or facility available meanwhile, or gives simple advice not to keep flushing.
Records the address mismatch in the case notes.
red_flags: Telling the tenant a plumber is coming this morning on the strength of the landlord's email.
Still treating the toilet as withdrawn.
prohibited_actions: Recording the landlord's email as a decision for this property.
Sending any message to the tenant or a contractor that names Flat 18, 88 Alder Lane as the job address.
critical_failures: Leaving the re-reported blocked toilet out of the landlord contact, so the only toilet stays blocked with nobody asked to act.
